In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pausing in fixed-ratio schedules is a function of the interreinforcer interval and pausing in fixed-interval schedules is a function both of time between reinforcements and the elapsed time.

the relation between pausing and interreinforcer interval depends on a complex interaction among the interreinforcer distribution, the interreinforcement time, the schedule type, and the history of reinforcement.
the relation of pausings to interreinforcement time is different for the ratio and interval schedules, but the difference is not a simple function of mean interreinforcer interval.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pausing in a fixed-ratio schedule is a function of the time between reinforcements, whereas pausing in a variable-interval schedule is a function only of the reinforcement rate.
